findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the hot holding units in the back of the cook line and part of the one on the cook line to not be holding temperature within the appropriate temperature range. PIC mention that the unit in question sometimes malfunction with temperature holding. They will work on getting an upgrade to a more functional unit. Ensure that these units is repair and calibrated to constantly hold the appropriate temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(A) The jug of milk in the chest cooler that holds the ice cream condiments was observed to not be date marked properly. Discussed with PIC. PIC told inspector that the milk was opened the previous day. PIC instructed a staff member to properly date mark the milk jug. The jug was dated immediately. Ensure that all food items not used be properly date marked if it is going to be stored for more that 24 hour after opening. 


Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed staff barehandling ready to eat food items during food prep. Discussed with PIC and an education was carried out to correct the behavior. Ensure that staff are aware to don gloves after handwashing before prepping ready to eat food at all times.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Observed quat sanitizer in all of the sani buckets to have a concentration between 0 and 100 ppm. findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) Observed sauteet mushrooms to have a temperature of 110 degrees. The mushrooms had been placed in the hot holding approximately 3 hours prior. The mushrooms were immediately heated to a temperature of 165 degrees F or higher. Additionally, more water was added to the steam table the mushrooms were on and the temperature was turned up.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111  (Pf) Observed live cockroaches on glue traps during the inspection near the dish machine. Additionally, there were dead cockroaches under the ice cream machine. The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate cockroaches, using proper pest control processes as needed. It is recommended to punch holes in walls to determine the source of the cockroaches. When that is completed, the holes must be cleaned and filled. Reference 6-501.111.

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.citation_text:
750.210 - Pot roast in reheating/hot holding unit on cook line had surface temperature of 94F and internal temperature of 104F-106F. Employee doing prep stated he got the foods in the unit to reheat after he arrived for work around 8a. It was 10a when temperature was checked. Mashed potatoes and BBQ pork had internal temperatures of 155F; 157F respectively. All three pans were moved to the flat grill to rapidly finish heating the foods to 165F. Smaller portions of beef and chicken gravy were already +170F.
Potentially hazardous foods shall be reheated rapidly to 165F/higher throughout the product. Properly reheat food to 165F/above.

**Make sure water is in the reheating/hot holding units prior to placing foods inside to reheat. Thick foods, such as roast and BBQ pork, will heat faster in smaller portions. Also, using a single pan, instead of double pan, when initially heating foods will help heat foods quicker. It is important to stir foods frequently to help heat evenly throughout the products. Staff and management need to monitor the products during heating process to ensure foods are reaching 165F within 2 hrs. After reheating is completed, then a double pan method could be used for hot holding (to help avoid burning of foods in pans) as long as the system being used is maintaining foods 135F/above during hot holding.**

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
750.140b - Pans of brown gravy, chicken gravy, and chili in walkin cooler had surface temperatures of 63F-65F and internal temperatures of 78F-83F. Manager noted the products were removed from reheat station around 12-12:30p, but time was not marked anywhere on labels of cooling foods. Manager was given option to immediately reheat for use or discard foods. All three products were already past the first two hours of cooling time frame and were voluntarily discarded. 
Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F win 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F/below w/in an additional 4 hrs. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. Utilize ice baths and stir foods frequently to rapidly cool foods to benchmark temperatures in the designated time frame for proper cooing. The only way to know a food is properly cooling is to use a clean, calibrated stem thermometer for monitoring temperatures during cooling process. Foods can be left uncovered during cooling process as long as shelves above are clean and no raw foods (raw meats; unwashed produced) are stored above cooling foods. Label cooling foods with date and time. **Rapid chill handout provided**

Until repairs are made to the wall mounted dispenser at the 3 part sink the quat sanitizer in the mop closet will be utilized for making sanitizer buckets and will also be transferred to 3 part sink for any manual ware washing that may need to be done.
Check the dispenser daily to ensure sanitizer is dispensed at proper concentration (200ppm). 
Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
750.800 - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled with food or general buildup:
A) bottom under drawers in make line cooler (food debris; lids to pans) and
B) sprayers at 3 part sink and sink next to dish machine - crevices on sprayer surface with buildup.
Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - A) Single use gloves were observed stored outside of boxes. Gloves in back next to reheat station had debris on them. Management was advised on proper storage of gloves (educational handout provided). It is ideal to leave single use gloves in the original packaging. If for some reason the packaging is damaged and/or inhibiting the easy removal of gloves for use then gloves should be stored in a clean, sanitized and covered container to protect gloves from potential contamination. 
B) Plastic bowls were observed outside of packaging on dry storage shelf. Manager placed bowls back inside packaging to protect the food contact surface of the bowls.
All single use articles shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects items from potential contamination.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1300 - Spray bottle of clear liquid in mop closet was not labeled. Chlorine test strip was used to verify it was a bleach solution that was almost pure bleach (test strip showed concentration to be off the chart - test strip was bleached out). Manager on duty emptied the solution into the mopsink to correct the violation.
Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Maintain proper labels on spray bottles.
Use chlorine test strips to verify concentration is not stronger than 100-200ppm in spray bottles used for wiping down surfaces.
